PASS with disclosures (batch_130). 21 rows = 3 items x 7 response levels; validate_items.R --table-sets passes on both sets (Hope_1/Hope_2/Hope_3; resp 1-7; live table 3,030 rows = 1,010 per item at waves 0 and 5). (1) INSTRUMENT (Step 3b). The live data is the 3-item hope facet of the CPC-12 (Compound Psychological Capital questionnaire, Lorenz, Beer, Puetz & Heinitz 2016, PLOS ONE 11(4):e152892). Confirmed three ways: data/pellerin2020_covid_resources.py melts exactly [f'Hope_{i}' for i in range(1,4)] and names the CPC-12 in its comment; Pellerin & Raufaste (2020) state hope was assessed with the CPC-12 and quote as their example item 'If I should find myself in a jam, I could think of many ways to get out of it', which is CPC-12 item 1 verbatim; and the live 1-7 range matches the paper's stated uniform 1='strongly disagree' to 7='strongly agree' format (the CPC-12's own studies used 1-6). No mismatch. (2) TEXT SOURCE. The OSF deposit (osf.io/45aq3) holds only PsyR_lockdown2020.R and data.PsyR_lockdown2020.csv; the CSV header carries bare codes (Hope_1..Hope_3, GQ_1.., Cog_1..) and no variable labels, and the R script is analysis-only. The Frontiers article has no supplementary material and reproduces one example item per scale. So the wording ships from the instrument's own publication: the CPC-12 S1 Appendix (doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0152892.s001, CC BY 4.0), whose hope block is items 1-3, transcribed verbatim including the trailing full stops. Those three are the State Hope Scale's items 1, 4 and 5 (the appendix marks them SHS1/SHS4/SHS5). (3) LANGUAGE / FALLBACK. The study was run in French: participants were recruited in France, those living outside France were excluded, and the paper names French versions of its other instruments. The administered French CPC-12 wording is NOT recoverable in scope - it is in neither the OSF deposit (checked: both files, no French item text, only codes) nor the paper or its supplements (there are none). So this takes the documented fallback: English in the base fields, _translated columns omitted, language='French', text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=official_instrument_english (the CPC-12 authors' own English parallel version). (4) OPTIONS. The paper publishes only the two anchors, 1='strongly disagree' and 7='strongly agree'. Points 2-6 were left BLANK rather than padded with their own numbers. Direction confirmed against the data: all three items are positively worded, intercorrelate positively (.46-.64) and correlate positively with every well-being scale (.20 to .61), and Hope_1 sits at 5.56/7 - consistent with 7 = agree, not the reverse. The anchor strings are also the paper's English for French anchors, i.e. the same fallback as the item text. (5) MAPPING. mapping_basis=paper_order. The IRW codes ARE the deposit's column names, but that deposit has no labels, so the tie Hope_k <-> CPC-12 hope item k is a number-to-number order inference that nothing states. Verified against the data - see verification_pellerin2020_cpc_hope.csv and verify_pellerin2020_cpc_hope.R; status VERIFIED. (6) RIGHTS. Not blocked. The CPC-12 wording is published in a CC BY 4.0 PLOS ONE appendix by its own developers; the upstream originator of these three items is Snyder et al.'s State Hope Scale (1996, JPSP 70:321-335), and no reserved-right clause - fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution - could be located or quoted for either the CPC-12 or the State Hope Scale. Per the standing rule, silence is permission and a restriction that cannot be quoted does not fire. instrument_rights_register.csv carries no CPC-12, PsyCap or Hope Scale row as of 2026-09-10. RETRY TEST: n/a - this is a clean pass, not a block. The one thing left open is the administered French wording; an unchanged retry would NOT recover it (determinate: neither the deposit nor the paper published it), so recovering it would need a French CPC-12 validation source located off-source, which is a later backfill pass, not a retry.
